bib.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality

question: How can the Skip-gram word-vector model be made faster and more accurate, and extended from words to idiomatic phrases?
hypothesis: Subsampling frequent words and a simplified NCE (negative sampling) speed up training and improve vectors, and treating phrases as single tokens captures non-compositional meanings.
contributions: Subsampling of frequent words: faster training and better rare-word vectors
Negative sampling, a simple alternative to hierarchical softmax
Data-driven phrase finding and phrase vectors, with a phrase analogy test set

method.summary: Skip-gram trained with hierarchical softmax (Huffman tree), NCE or negative sampling, with optional frequent-word subsampling, on a 1B-word news corpus; phrases are found by a bigram score and merged into single tokens. Evaluated on word and phrase analogy tasks and by nearest-neighbour inspection.

datasets.name: internal Google news dataset
datasets.size: one billion words (about 1B; 33B and 6B-word variants for the best phrase model)
datasets.preprocessing: words occurring less than 5 times discarded, vocabulary 692K; phrases merged into single tokens for phrase experiments

models.name: Skip-gram (NEG-5, NEG-15, NCE-5, HS-Huffman)
models.architecture: Skip-gram with input and output vectors v_w, v'_w, no dense matrix multiplication

models.name: Collobert and Weston, Turian et al., Mnih and Hinton vectors

training.objective: maximize average log p(w_{t+j}|w_t) over window c; p via full softmax, hierarchical softmax (Huffman tree) or negative sampling log sigma(v'_wO^T v_wI) + sum_k E log sigma(-v'_wi^T v_wI)
training.tokens: about 1B words (33B for best phrase model, 6B for the smaller one)
training.regularisation: subsampling of frequent words, discard probability 1 - sqrt(t/f(w)), t typically around 10^-5
training.wall_clock: Table 1 times in minutes (38 min NEG-5 without subsampling); over 100 billion words in one day on one machine

other.phrase_score: (count(wi wj) - delta) / (count(wi) x count(wj)); delta discount, threshold not stated
other.context_size_c: 5 in experiments; best phrase model uses entire sentence

inference.decoding: nearest neighbour by cosine distance, input words excluded

metrics.definition: analogy a:b::c:? correct if nearest vector (cosine) to vec(b)-vec(a)+vec(c) is the answer

limits: Single runs, no seeds or variance; accuracies are on the authors' own analogy sets
Training corpus (internal Google news) is not public, so the 1B and 33B-word results cannot be rerun exactly
Optimizer, learning rate, schedule, subsampling per-run details and phrase threshold and delta are not stated
Subsampling formula and U^(3/4) noise distribution chosen heuristically; the NEG vs HS ranking flips with subsampling and hyperparameters are task specific
Noise distribution comparison is 'not reported here'
Phrase detection by bigram score only; other phrase-finding techniques not compared
Nearest-neighbour comparisons with older models (Table 6) are qualitative, and the Skip-gram model used 2-3 orders of magnitude more data
Static word vectors: no context-dependent meaning (dated by later contextual models)

terms.definition: a simplified NCE objective that distinguishes the target word from k draws of a noise distribution using logistic regression, using only samples
each word w_i in the training set is discarded with probability P(w_i)=1-sqrt(t/f(w_i))
binary tree over the output layer with words as leaves, needing about log2(W) node evaluations; Huffman tree used
